page: Microsoft Azure E16ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv5 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The server features 16 dedicated vCPUs, which map to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The processor includes a 48 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, Intel Deep Learning Boost (AVX-512 VNNI), and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

This instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage capabilities include a bundled 614 GB local disk, and the server is Premium Storage capable, allowing integration with high-performance external storage. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this configuration.

Benchmark data places the E16ds_v5 in the average performance tier across most compute and memory metrics. It achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1642.0 and a multi-core score of 10078.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 21234.25. In database and memory-intensive operations, the server processed 15.92 million Redis SET operations per second and scored 7992.24 on Passmark database operations. Notably, the server demonstrated strong performance in small-model LLM text generation, reaching 289.27 tokens per second with a 135M parameter model, though performance scales down to 12.36 tokens per second for a medium 7B model.

The E16ds_v5 offers a balanced qualitative cost-efficiency profile for memory-intensive workloads, leveraging its high memory density and bundled local storage to reduce the need for external disk allocations. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention. This server is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, software compilation, and medium-scale web serving or data processing tasks.
